conditions.text: Preconditions to set up: app 1.2.0, iOS 18.4, iPhone15,2.

The packet also records profile.consistent = false from module1.profile across both events, so the captured profile is flagged as not internally consistent; the packet does not explain what that inconsistency is.

Push state is not required to reproduce: across the two events push.deliverable was true in one and false in the other, push.os_permission was ALLOWED in one and DENIED in the other, and push.provider_registration was REGISTERED in one and STALE in the other.
Note the evidence base is small: only 2 events were considered.
Commit a6af0bd ("Clean up router") touches src/app/router.ts, the same file as the culprit frame, so it is a lead worth checking when setting up the build, not a confirmed cause.

missing_evidence_questions.text: How was the navigation to /legacy/inbox initiated (deep link, in-app tap, push open)? The packet records only the navigation target, not its trigger.
What does profile.consistent = false mean for this incident, and which attributes disagreed?
Did commit a6af0bd remove or rename the /legacy/inbox route in src/app/router.ts, and does the failure disappear on a build before it?
Does the error reproduce on other app versions, OS versions or devices, or only on the single configuration seen in these two events?
Given push-related fields differ between the two events, is there any path where push state affects routing, or is it purely incidental?

steps_prose.text: Run app version 1.2.0 on iOS 18.4 on an iPhone15,2 (device model iPhone15,2), which is the configuration present in both events.
Trigger a navigation to the route /legacy/inbox; this is the only user step captured, and it appears in all events considered.
Observe the failure: resolveRoute (src/app/router.ts:31) raises Error "No route matches /legacy/inbox".

summary.text: Two Sentry events show an Error "No route matches /legacy/inbox" thrown from resolveRoute in src/app/router.ts line 31 when the app navigates to /legacy/inbox.
